# Purpose

`analyze_sales.R` summarises revenue, profit and margin by product category for a synthetic retail transactions dataset. It saves the summary as a CSV file and as a bar chart so the results can be reused without re-running the analysis.

# Inputs

The script reads one file, `data/retail_transactions.csv`, with these columns:

```{r inputs-table, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
inputs <- data.frame(
  Column = c("order_id", "date", "product", "category", "region",
             "units", "price", "discount", "cost", "channel"),
  Type = c("text", "date", "text", "text", "text",
           "integer", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "text"),
  Description = c("Unique order identifier", "Order date (YYYY-MM-DD)",
                  "Product name", "Product category", "Sales region",
                  "Units sold", "Price per unit before discount",
                  "Discount as a fraction of price", "Cost per unit",
                  "Sales channel (Store, Online, Phone)")
)
knitr::kable(inputs)
```

Required packages: `readr`, `dplyr` and `ggplot2`.

# Outputs

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `output/category_summary.csv` | Orders, units, revenue, profit and margin for each category |
| `output/revenue_by_category.png` | Horizontal bar chart of revenue by category |

# Example usage

Run the script from the project root:

```r

```

# Notes

- Only synthetic data is used.
- Margin is profit divided by revenue, rounded to three decimals.
